change: the Command Center's Unit 3 speaks the CED's numbers, in the CED's order
_context: Unit 3 was renumbered onto the CED on 2026-08-28 and the six live lesson pages
moved that day. The Command Center did not. Measured live 2026-09-09: its rows
read 3.1 to 3.6 on the retired site numbering, with a second CED badge beside
each title, while units 1, 2, 4 and 5 key on the CED number and carry no badge
at all. There is a row 3.6 and the CED's Unit 3 stops at 3.5.
The unit note still told teachers the sequence differs from the CED's topic
order. That stopped being true when the three-cycle moved the bodies: handle
order IS CED order now, lesson-1 through lesson-6 stating 3.1a, 3.1b, 3.2, 3.3,
3.4, 3.5. Three rows also opened the wrong page, which is board 283; keying a
row on the CED number makes the handle follow from it, so that fix lands here
as a consequence and the sheet in imports/2026-09-08-cyber-cc-unit3-relink/ is
A teacher's taught ticks live in localStorage keyed on the row id, so the sheet
carries a one-time remap. Without it a tick on 3.3 Firewalls would come back

checks.name: CED numbers, CED order, right handles, ticks that follow their lessons
the relink suite this supersedes still passes, so the two do not disagree
every row's number matches the lesson page it opens
checks._why: Reads NEITHER source the generator is built on: not lib/cyber-unit3-renumber.js PLAN, not config/cyber-topics.json. It asks each LIVE page what it is through the data-lesson-id the gradebook keys on, and compares that to the number the row displays. Against the live page before the import this answers id-matches-page=0, so the assertion below is FALSE beforehand and cannot pass on a page that never changed. Run --fixed for the pre-merge gate, which fetches live and applies the sheet in memory; run it with no arguments after the import, when it observes the deployed page directly.

checks.name: the sheet parses back to exactly what the transform produced from live
checks._why: Generation is not evidence that generation worked. The CSP sheet lost 90 bytes a page while every semantic check passed. Reads the shipped CSV back through a parser and diffs against a fresh transform of the live body.

checks.name: M1 THE PING-PONG: the row rewrite reads the number already in the handle
checks._why: The trap lib/cyber-unit3-renumber.js documents. A cycle written as ordered replaces moves rows that were already right and cannot tell its own output from its input.
checks.replace: for (const q of ROWS) out = out.split(`lesson-${q.target}`).join(`lesson-${q.target === 6 ? 1 : q.target + 1}`);
checks.expect_failure: data array: every row opens the lesson its id names

checks.name: M2 the map is typed by hand instead of derived from PLAN
checks._why: Retyping the Unit 3 mapping is how site 3.3 and 3.4 became each other's CED topics in the first place.
checks.expect_failure: every ROW comes from a PLAN entry

checks.name: M3 the rows are left in their old order instead of CED order
checks._why: Reordering is half the fix. Ids alone would leave the list reading 3.1a, 3.1b, 3.4, 3.3, 3.5, 3.2 and contradict the order the six pages actually run in.
checks.expect_failure: the rows read 3.1a, 3.1b, 3.2, 3.3, 3.4, 3.5 in that order

checks.name: M4 the CED badge is stripped from the 3.1 pair too
checks._why: 3.1a and 3.1b are the two rows whose id is NOT the CED topic number, so they are the two that still need the badge to say which topic they belong to.

checks.name: M5 the badge is kept everywhere, so four rows repeat their own id
checks.find:
if (r.newId === r.cedTopic) out = out.replace(/,\s*ced:"CED 3\.\d"/, '');
  else out = out.replace(/(\bced:")CED 3\.\d(")/, `$1CED ${r.cedTopic}$2`);
checks.expect_failure: drops the badge that would repeat its own id

checks.name: M6 the tick migration applies the map IN PLACE, so the 3.3/3.4 swap ping-pongs
checks._why: This is the mutation that found a hollow assertion. With every tick set to `true` the in-place rewrite still left one of the swapped pair looking correct and the battery came back green. The ticks in the suite now carry DISTINCT values that name their lesson, and it reds on the rule it targets.

checks.expect_failure: a tick on firewalls stays on firewalls

checks.find:
out = addTaughtMigration(out);
  if (out === null) return null;

checks.name: M8 the note is left as it was, still telling teachers the order differs from the CED
checks.find: newBlock = newBlock.replace(noteRe, (m, head, old, tail) => head + NOTE + tail);
checks.replace: newBlock = newBlock.replace(noteRe, (m, head, old, tail) => head + old + tail);
checks.expect_failure: the unit note no longer claims a sequence differing from the CED

checks.name: M9 the STU link map keys are renumbered but the handles inside are not
checks._why: Two blocks carry these links and both have to move. Fixing only one is the failure this separates: the data array and the link map are asserted independently.
checks.expect_failure: link map: every row opens the lesson its id names

checks.name: M10 the row boundary goes greedy, so one row's text swallows the rows after it
checks.expect_failure: the rows read 3.1a, 3.1b, 3.2, 3.3, 3.4, 3.5 in that order

checks.name: M12 the derived lesson id drifts from config/cyber-topics.json
checks._why: Disabling the cross-check alone is VACUOUS while the two sources agree, so it was replaced with one that makes them disagree. That is the only condition the check exists for.
checks.expect_failure: crossCheck finds nothing to complain about

_withdrawn.name: M11 the one-shot precondition is removed
_withdrawn._why: WITHDRAWN because it came back GREEN, and a green mutation run is a failed check rather than a passing one. Refusing an already-renumbered page turns out to be defended three times over: disable the explicit precondition and the row-id regex refuses on the new id shape; widen that too and the PLAN lookup finds no row for the retired ids. No single-line mutation isolates any one guard, so the suite's assertion 8 is LABELLED as insurance against a future widening rather than as something a passing run establishes. Recorded here rather than deleted, so the next session does not spend the afternoon rediscovering it.
